title: Workflows and agents: who owns the control flow?

items.stem: Which statement best tells a workflow apart from an agent?

options.text: A workflow calls tools, while an agent only writes text
A workflow calls the model once, while an agent calls it often
A workflow's code sets the steps, while an agent's model sets them
A workflow uses a small model, while an agent uses a large one

items.stem: Four designs for parts of a makerspace assistant are described below. Which one is an agent rather than a workflow?

options.text: Code asks the model to label each question, then sends it to one of two fixed prompts
The model picks between searching manuals, checking the calendar or asking the student, and repeats until done
Code looks up the machine, then asks the model to summarize that machine's manual page
Code runs three model calls in a set order: extract the date, check the calendar, write the reply

items.stem: Every booking request goes through the same four steps in the same order: read the request, check the calendar, reserve the slot, confirm to the student. What is the strongest reason to build this as a fixed workflow rather than an agent?

options.text: Agents cannot call calendar tools, so only code can check availability
A workflow lets the model choose the step order, which makes bookings more flexible
An agent is allowed only one tool, but a booking needs more than one
The steps are known in advance, so fixed code is cheaper and more predictable

items.stem: In a workflow, what decides which step runs next after a model call finishes?

A booking workflow makes exactly 2 model calls per request. An agent doing the same job averages 5 model calls per request, because it decides each step itself. Over 200 requests, how many more model calls does the agent make than the workflow?

The assistant has two jobs. Booking always follows the same steps. Troubleshooting a failed print needs a different next lookup depending on what the previous lookup found. With a small model budget, which design is best?

options.text: Booking as a fixed workflow, troubleshooting as an agent
Both jobs as agents, so one design covers everything
Booking as an agent, troubleshooting as a fixed workflow
Both jobs as fixed workflows, so the cost is always lowest
